attributes.law_screen: claim.law.chained-init-constant-share.20260829.v1: SCREENED, correctly diagnosed the cluster, and TRIED TWICE -- both spellings measured identically and are recorded as a dead axis; see residual for why the law's prescription does not close this instance. claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge.20260831.v1: SCREENED and DECISIVE for classification -- I confirmed by target offsets that this is the FORWARD variant (the conditional at 0x124 targets 0x12c, one past the unconditional at 0x128, whose own target 0x130 is the loop-increment block ahead of it, and that block is genuinely reached from elsewhere via the `beq ->130` at 0xec). The law therefore says the axis SHOULD be workable, and its prescribed spelling -- a guard whose body is a single control transfer -- was tried as `if (best > value) { continue; }` and compiled BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the existing `if (best <= value) { best = value; }`, leaving the --ops clusters bit-for-bit unchanged. That is a genuine boundary case for the law and is flagged here for its author. claim.law.if-else-arm-swap-controls-fallthrough-placement.20260831.v1: SCREENED, explicitly NOT applicable on its own stated boundary -- one arm is empty, so there are not two statement bodies of differing size to swap. claim.law.value-identity-split-completes-a-broken-recolor-bijection.20260831.v1: SCREENED and it names the second cluster (see residual), but in the REVERSE direction from the law's subject: here OUR build carries the extra split and the target does not. claim.law.insn-count-parity-outranks-local-opcode-fidelity.20260831.v1: APPLIED as the arbiter, and it is what stopped the chained-init form being banked -- see verification. claim.law.shared-level-scaled-base-refuses-member-form.20260831.v1: SCREENED and HONOURED -- WorldOpen's `(u8*)(requirement * 2) + (s32)p + character*CHAR_SAVE_STRIDE + COMPLETION2_OFF` is exactly the law's protected level-scaled byte-pointer shape (target confirms it: `slwi r26,r24,1` then `lhax r0,r26,r0`), so it was left raw and never pushed to member form.
attributes.residual: real 40, insns 99/99, opcode multiset DIFFERS by 8 tokens: target-only +2 addi +1 b +1 ble, ours-only -1 bgt -2 li -1 mr. THREE clusters. (1) SHARED ZERO @0xc8-0xe0: target materialises the zero ONCE (`li r27,0` into best) and COPIES it into both the loop counter and the strength-reduced byte offset (`addi r28,r27,0`, `addi r30,r27,0`); ours emits three independent `li rX,0`. The source already spells the sharing (`best = 0; for (player = best; ...)`) and MWCC still splits it. (2) VALUE-IDENTITY SPLIT @0xc4-0xd8: target loads `requirement` straight into its callee-saved home (`lwz r24,0(r3)`) and derives the doubled index from that home (`slwi r26,r24,1`); ours loads into r0, keeps r0 for the shift (`slwi r28,r0,1`) and pays a separate `mr r24,r0` to home it -- an ours-only copy, the mirror image of the usual home-copy law. (3) BRANCH PAIR @0x124: target `ble ->12c; b ->130` (empty block between) where ours fuses to `bgt ->130`; classified FORWARD variant by target-offset inspection, so it is nominally source-reachable, but the law's prescribed spelling reproduces our fused form exactly.
